newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, March 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, March 13.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Thursday.
- A presidential election in November looked a virtual certainty last night after Mary Robinson announced she would not seek a second seven-year term in office.
- Woodchester set to seek tenders for its takeover.
- Intel to build new updating PCs in Ireland - IBEC chief lashes public pay policy warning saying that the time had come to draw a line in the sand follwing the settlement of the nurses pay row.
- Consumers in Ireland rate honesty and professionalism ahead of service when it comes to buying life assurance and pension products.
- United Distillers is expected to spend over five million punts on the develoment of its new spirits brand, legalised Irish poitin.
- A bomb disposal team is moved to the border fulltime after the attempted bomb attack by loyalists in Monaghan.
- Extradition proceedings against Roisin McAliskey could continue into next year.
- Foundation built for peace in Northern Ireland, deputy prime minister Dick Spring said.
- Offaly county council has been granted an interim injunction in the high court preventing ESAT Digifone from completing work on the installation of a steel cabin and antennae.
- Aer Lingus told to submit proposals on alliance which could involve selling part of the airline by the end of the year.
- Building industry forecast to grow by 10.5 percent
